Because offset/user_count/members all come from whichever response resolves last, an out-of-order resolution leaves the model showing one page's members with another page's offset and page indicator. The mechanism is fully verifiable in the diff (group.js findMembers setProperties; controller actions next/previous/addMembers/removeMember).

adjudication.rationale: In Discourse.Group#findMembers the AJAX promise always `.then` calls `self.setProperties({ user_count, limit, offset, members: ... })` based on the response (group.js). Multiple UI actions (`next`/`previous` in admin-group.js.es6, and `addMembers`/`removeMember` which call `findMembers()` again after their own requests) can trigger overlapping `findMembers()` calls without any abort/sequencing/token check. If requests resolve out of order, an older response can overwrite `offset`/`members`/`user_count` with stale values, making pagination state and displayed members inconsistent.
